Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Medicore is progressing toward a formal pilot for EU-only inference for our clinical decision-support workload. Before we loop legal and procurement, we need concrete answers for a few items so our security team can complete the SCCs risk matrix:

- Control plane residency: will the control plane for a Private/VPC deployment ever leave the EU (metadata, management calls)?
- Operator access: what are the exact conditions and methods by which Redwood personnel may access EU-hosted inference nodes (jumpbox, bastion, or operator sessions)? Auditability?
- Backups and backups restoration: where are snapshots stored, retention policy, and how are they encrypted?
- KMS and key ownership: can we bring our own CMK in-region or must keys be in Redwood-managed KMS?
- Cross-border failover: if an EU region is degraded, what is the fallback behavior and can that be blocked for EU-only customers?

Attached is our initial SCCs checklist with highlighted rows — can you confirm items and give a tentative timeline to deliver an evidence package (attestation + logs)? We are targeting an internal sign-off meeting on 2027-12-15.

Hi Sophie — thanks for the clear list. I attached an annotated diff (quick pass) and a high-level control-plane diagram. Short answers up-front so you can triage:

- Control plane: metadata/control-plane APIs for Private (VPC) customers remain within EU control plane endpoints; management plane telemetry that we collect is stored in the customer region by default for EU-only customers, and never routed to US control planes unless explicitly authorized in contract.
- Operator access: we require documented authorization for operator sessions. For EU-only Private installs we support session-based access via audited jumpbox with dual-approval and session recording.
- Backups: snapshots can be configured to remain in-region; default retention 90 days for inference artifacts unless customer requests shorter retention; encrypted at rest with CMKs.
- KMS: BYOK is available for Dedicated/Private customers with keys in our supported EU KMS providers; Redwood can also provision keys if needed.
- Failover: we offer configurable failover policies — by default we will not failover outside the region for EU-only contracts; we can also implement manual failover gates.

Karthik and Naomi — can you confirm the operational and attestation granularity and a realistic delivery date for an evidence bundle? Sophie — I propose a call Thursday 12/2 to run through the checklist and agree on which items need a formal attestation vs. an operational runbook.

Hi all — tagging in a few technical clarifications and what we can commit to in our evidence bundle:

1) Control plane and telemetry: For Private (VPC) deployments we run a customer-dedicated control plane in the EU region you select. Control-plane logs (API calls, ops events) are written to an S3-equivalent in-region bucket with encryption and can be exported to your SIEM.

2) Operator access & sessions: Operator access to inference hosts is via a centralized bastion in the same region. Access requires two-person approval and sessions are recorded; recordings and command logs can be delivered as part of an audit package. We do not perform interactive shell access without documented cause and approval.

3) Backups & snapshots: Snapshots of model cache, KV store, and system state are encrypted with the CMK you provide (BYOK supported). Snapshots are stored in-region by default. We can provide a list of snapshot manifests and deletion receipts for the evidence bundle.

4) Key management: BYOK is supported for Cloud KMS providers in the EU (Azure Key Vault, Google KMS, AWS KMS in eu-* regions). If you want an HSM-backed BYOK, we can discuss options (longer lead time).

5) Failover behavior: Our deployment orchestration supports configurable isolation policies. For EU-only contracts we can set a strict policy that prevents automated cross-border failover; manual escalation is required and logged.

Operational evidence we can provide by 2027-12-10 if we lock scope today:
- Control plane audit logs (last 90 days)
- Bastion session recordings for any operator access used during onboarding
- Snapshot manifests + encryption metadata
- KMS key wrapping proof (KMIP/PKCS#11 metadata)

I will prepare a short runbook describing how operator access is requested, approved, and executed. That runbook will include the jumpbox flow, approval emails, and log locations.

-Karthik

Hi Sophie — appreciate the specifics. A few legal/compliance notes from the SCCs/Schrems II perspective:

- Attestation vs. evidence: Medicore will need both an operational attestation (signed statement from Redwood covering the control plane residency, operator access rules, and encryption posture) and machine-readable evidence (logs, manifests). The attestation should reference the specific SCC clauses and state whether Redwood is an exporter or data processor for metadata and inference artifacts.

- Subprocessors & contract language: Please flag any subprocessor that may have access to metadata (monitoring vendors, backup storage providers). We'll propose a short addendum to the MSA that enumerates subprocessors and the restriction that they must process within the EU for EU-only contracts.

- Retention and deletion: The SCCs assessment will expect a documented deletion/verifiable erasure process for snapshots and backups. We should include the deletion receipts and a timeline for irrevocable deletion.

Action items I can own: draft the attestation template (legal language mapped to SCCs), list required evidence artifacts, and propose MSA addendum language for subprocessors and failover restrictions. I aim to deliver the draft attestation and evidence checklist by 2027-12-09.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
